human_tolerance.notes: Breeds in farm ponds, borrow pits and other disturbed wetlands as well as forest pools (Wikipedia, Geographic range and habitat).

phases.name: dormancy
phases.note: Northern populations hibernate under logs or behind loose bark; the Gulf Coast populations are not represented by this single country-level phase.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: Northern populations breed March to June as the warm rains start (Wikipedia, Reproduction). Southern populations breed October to March and are not represented by this phase.

vocalizations.description: Males sound a short, high-pitched peep from the edges of breeding ponds, calling roughly 15 to 25 times a minute through the evening and night; the chorus is among the first in spring and its rate rises with warmth.

AmphibiaWeb id omitted: the page did not resolve.

common_names.note: English 'Spring Peeper' and Dutch 'kruisboomkikker' Wikidata labels; Wikipedia uses 'spring peeper'.

conservation.note: Wikidata P141 = least concern (Q211005). Wikipedia: no special status in most areas.

range.note: Wikipedia: widespread through the eastern United States and eastern Canada, Gulf Coast to the Atlantic provinces and west to Saskatchewan. Native: US, CA. Country-level only; no introduced range recorded.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Walks and hops in low vegetation; swims in breeding ponds. Climb is omitted: the toepads allow climbing but the shared anuran program has no climb pose, and the species mostly hunts in low vegetation (Wikipedia, Diet).

traits.skin.note: 'Moist' is the format's amphibian skin class; the source describes the colour and adaptable pigmentation, not the skin texture.

traits.respiration.note: Lungs (Wikipedia, Respiratory and circulatory system: air forced from the lungs through the larynx to the vocal sac).

traits.metamorphosis.note: Aquatic tadpole stage then metamorphosis into a frog (Wikipedia, Lifecycle).

traits.nest_type.note: Eggs laid singly or in small groups and hidden under vegetation or debris at the water base; no nest.

traits.perching.note: Calls can come from shrub or grass bases and from arboreal positions, but the species is not a perching animal in the schema sense.

traits.mass_kg.note: Midpoint of the 3 to 5 g adult mass range in Wikipedia, Description.

traits.length_m.note: Midpoint of the 18 to 38 mm body length range in Wikipedia, Description (males 18 to 30 mm, females 20 to 35 mm). Not a measured mean.

traits.lifespan_y.note: Wikipedia, Lifespan: 'can live an estimated three years in the wild'. This is an estimate, not a population mean.

traits.diet.note: Wikipedia lists only small invertebrates for adults (beetles, ants, flies, spiders) and does not report vertebrate prey, so 1.0 invertebrate is an authored allocation. Tadpoles are suspension feeders on algae and detritus; not modelled.

traits.social.note: Authored: solitary outside breeding. Breeding choruses of several hundred males and females aggregate at ponds (Wikipedia, Geographic range and habitat), which the Solitary structure does not express.

traits.activity_pattern.note: Wikipedia, Diet: nocturnal insectivores emerging at night; deep damp forest populations also hunt by day. Males call from dusk through the night.

traits.defense.note: Authored: the sources describe colour change and calling but not a threat response. Flee matches the shared program's hop-away behaviour.

habitat.use.note: Authored split: mainly ground in forest leaf litter and low vegetation, with time in water during the breeding season.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: Non-breeding season: inhabits dead plant material in the woods (Wikipedia, Geographic range and habitat).

habitat.resources.note: Prey from Wikipedia Diet; ephemeral and semipermanent wetlands for breeding; logs and loose bark for hibernation. Weights are authored and no month restriction is set because the source season differs by latitude.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Breeds in farm ponds and borrow pits, and is 'very adaptable' with respect to habitat (Wikipedia). Adapter means it uses disturbed and suburban habitat, not that gardens are documented.

seasonal.strategy.note: Wikipedia, Geographic range and habitat: northern populations hibernate under logs or behind loose bark and tolerate freezing.

seasonal.triggers.note: Authored temperatures; no open source gives thresholds.

seasonal.phases.note: Breeding March to June is the northern population pattern in Wikipedia, Reproduction; the southern October to March pattern is not representable by one country-level phase. Dormancy is the northern winter window. Both are limitations for the Gulf Coast.

seasonal.life_stages.note: Tadpoles remain two to three months (75 days is the midpoint); the species breeds in its third spring, about 2 years old (Wikipedia, Lifespan). Egg duration has no source and is omitted; scales are authored.

vocalizations.peep.note: Calling rate 15 to 25 calls per minute gives cooldown 3 s (60 / 20). Months are the early-spring calling window in Wikipedia, Mate searching behavior. Loudness and time windows are authored.

look.note: Tan, grey or brown with a dark cross on the back, pale yellow inner thighs (Wikipedia, Description); proportions and palette are authored. Toepads are not modelled.

behavior.note: Shared nocturnal anuran program with the peep call id and default months; authored parameters. Calls outside March and April are not represented.
